# 14 — Glossary

Definitions written for a creator, in the order you meet them. Each says what the thing is, and — where
it is easy to get wrong — what it is **not**.

---

### `.relics`

One file describing one project: the generator, the trait schema, the market mapping, the collection
metadata and the digests that pin all of it. It is a sealed ZIP with its own magic string, and every
file inside is hash-declared so a launchpad can re-derive the whole thing rather than trust the
manifest.

A bundle describes a **project**, not a protocol release, and it never states a chain fact. It has no
field for a deployed address, a runtime codehash or a script pointer — those are refused by name if
you try. That is precisely what lets a bundle stay valid across a protocol generation change.

**A bundle requests; it never approves.** It can name the quote asset it wants and the launch method
it prefers. The chain decides.

---

### ProjectToken

Your project's ERC-20. Fixed supply, 18 decimals, minted once at launch. It is the asset your pool
trades and the asset that backs your artworks.

Not a governance token, not a claim on the protocol, and not something the platform takes a direct
share of — the platform's fee entitlement converts into the market's quote asset rather than sitting
in your token.

---

### ProjectCollection

Your project's ERC-721. It holds the art binding, answers `tokenURI(id)` for each artwork, and
answers `contractURI()` for the collection profile.

Its `owner()` is ERC-173 **attribution and permitted metadata control only**. It reads `ProjectRights`
directly, so it follows a sale of the project. It is not an upgrade authority and not a privileged
role over any escrow function.

---

### ProjectRights

A transferable ERC-721 that says who the creator of a project is. It carries the creator fee
entitlement — unclaimed and future — and it is what every metadata authority check resolves to.

**Transferring this token transfers the project.** There is no separate "sell the fee stream"
transaction; moving the token moves the stream. The contract publishes that warning on chain as a
constant so an interface can display the sentence the behaviour actually justifies rather than one it
wrote itself.

It cannot be destroyed: a transfer to the zero address is rejected on every path.

Rights authority is not protocol authority, in either direction. The rights owner governs the
project's metadata and receives its payouts and can never upgrade a contract. The protocol Safe can
upgrade the rights registry's code and can never mint rights, move rights, or redirect a payout.

---

### ArtHook

Your project's Uniswap v4 hook, deployed fresh at launch to a CREATE2 address whose low 14 bits
encode its permission mask. It does two jobs:

1. **It records your market's history** — swap counts, volumes, net flow, an organic price oracle —
   in bounded O(1) storage, which is what `tokenURI` reads at render time.
2. **It sets the pool's LP fee** — a real Uniswap v4 dynamic-fee override, returned per swap, which
   is the launch-protection schedule you elected.

It is permanently immutable: no proxy, no admin, no upgrade path. It carries no return-delta
permission, so it cannot take value out of a swap, and it reads nothing about who is swapping.

The current mask is in [02 — What a launch produces](02-what-a-launch-produces.md#the-hook). If you
have seen a different one, check which generation the document was describing before you copy it.

---

### Art runtime

Which engine renders your art, and what bytes that engine is given. Two exist: a registered
Solidity-SVG template driven by your configuration, and deterministic JavaScript stored on chain.

A bundle names the runtime and the keccak256 of the exact bytes it will be given, and a launch writes
that pair into the collection as the **art binding**. Nobody — including the platform — can swap your
art for different bytes afterwards.

**Approved is not launchable.** One list is what the bundle format accepts; the other is what the
launchpad actually binds and renders. A template on an approved-but-gated runtime ships and is
marked, never deleted and never presented as launchable.

---

### DNA

The immutable per-artwork seed derived at mint, from which every deterministic property of that
artwork follows. Same DNA plus same market state gives the same image, byte for byte, forever.

Not a trait table. Traits you attach are metadata; they do not determine the image.

---

### Market state

What your pool has actually done, as your hook recorded it: how much has been bought and sold, net
flow, how fragmented the activity was, the organic price history. It is an **input to the artwork**,
read at `tokenURI` time.

Two disciplines follow from that. Magnitude drives visual state, never count — a hundred dust swaps
and one large swap of the same total size must reach the same artistic state. And market state is
recorded from organic trades; the protocol's own settlement swaps are excluded so they cannot write
themselves into your art history.

---

### Quote asset

The asset your project is priced and traded in — the other leg of your canonical pool. Chosen at
launch and **immutable for the life of the project**, because it is written into the pool key and a
pool key is not writable by anyone.

Ethereum and Base admit only the canonical WETH. BNB Smart Chain admits WBNB — never call it WETH.
Robinhood Chain is the multi-quote chain and admits whatever the quote registry currently admits and
leaves enabled.

Disabling an asset in the registry blocks **new** launches against it and reaches nothing that has
already launched.

---

### Genesis liquidity

The single Uniswap v4 position minted in your launch transaction, directly against the `PoolManager`.
There is no LP token and no PositionManager NFT.

It is **single-sided**: your whole liquidity allocation of the project token, with **zero** quote
asset seeded by the project. So at launch there is executable ask liquidity and **no bid depth**
until real buyers put quote currency in. Nobody is obliged to buy, and no project-funded bootstrap
buy manufactures the appearance that somebody did.

The principal is held by an immutable custodian with no principal-withdrawal function, no migration
function and no upgrade path. Fee collection pokes the position at zero liquidity delta, so
collecting fees never moves principal — which is the design reason no withdrawal path is needed.

The honest claim is narrow: *genesis liquidity principal is held by the immutable locker and cannot
be withdrawn through the deployed locker.* Not "nobody can rug", which is unrestricted and false.

---

### Buy-and-entomb

Half of the platform's fee share is allocated to buying $RELICS on the open market and sending every
acquired token to the entombment address, permanently.

**It is not a burn.** Spendable and circulating supply fall; `totalSupply` does not change; no ERC-20
burn event occurs, because the deployed $RELICS token has no supply-decreasing path at all. All three
have to be said together — "we burn $RELICS" on its own implies a number goes down, and it does not.

**Allocated is not spent.** The allocation is made in the market's quote asset at collection and buys
$RELICS only once an approved route to WETH exists for that asset. Some quotes have none, so an
allocation can rest indefinitely. That is a normal state with its own status, not an error and not a
zero.

---

### Anti-snipe / launch protection

Whether the first minutes of your market are priced differently from every minute after them. A
creator election, made once, immutable afterwards, and declared by every launch:

- `NONE` — a flat base LP fee both ways from the first block. No window, no decay, no countdown, and
  **no protection**. A project on this mode must never be rendered as protected.
- `PROTECTED_98_MINUTES` — the buy-side LP fee starts high and decays to the base over the window;
  the sell side is the base fee throughout.
- `UNSPECIFIED` — the enum-zero sentinel. **Not a mode.** It means nobody chose, it is refused at
  bind, and rendering it as `NONE` turns an unset field into a deliberate choice nobody made.

It makes immediate acquisition expensive and removes the block-one speed advantage. It does **not**
guarantee equal allocation, identify anyone, or stop a buyer from waiting. Both halves of that
travel together — see [12 — Launch protection](12-launch-protection.md), which also lists the
phrasings that are false in either mode.

---

### `contractURI`

ERC-7572. The **collection profile**: name, description, cover, banner, links. Marketplace furniture.

On an RC6 collection it is the birth document — content-addressed, committed to by the launch, and
re-verified against that commitment on every read. It is non-empty in the launch receipt state, so
there is no second transaction to add it and nothing to poll for.

Not the artwork. See below.

---

### `tokenURI`

The **artwork**, per token. Base64 JSON with an embedded base64 SVG, computed on chain at read time
from the token's immutable DNA and live reads off your hook. No image file, no IPFS CID, no API, no
gateway in that path.

The one-line distinction worth memorising: **`contractURI` is the collection's profile; `tokenURI` is
the art.** Conflating them is how a project renders perfectly on chain and shows a blank tile
everywhere else.
